problem: Two places are wrong: 'The shape of a definition' (~line 11) and the PowerShell 5.1 bullet under 'The remote helpers' (~line 361). Both say that without quotes Kismet reads channels=1,6,11 as 'channels=1 plus two junk options, 6 and 11'.

If another option follows, it becomes part of that option's name: channels=1,6,11,mode=zigbee is read as channels=1 plus an option named '6,11,mode'. remote.py split_definition documents this, and the helper's warning says 'Kismet reads only its first item'.

problem: These pages describe the port lock as flock only and warn that it does not cross the container boundary. The places: Source-Definitions 'One board, one source' (~244-248); How-It-Works 'The port' (~127) and 'One board, one source' (~222, ~230); Firmware-Protocol 'One program at a time' (~34); Troubleshooting 'already in use' (~121); Docker-Reference (~378); Choosing-a-Setup (~79); Flashing-the-Firmware (~17); Guide-Updating (~33); Install-on-Raspberry-Pi (~395); Install-with-Docker (~306); Development-and-Testing 'Still to check' (~563).
correct: Both helpers take the flock and also put the tty in exclusive mode (TIOCEXCL). This is skipped only on a Linux pseudo-terminal. The kernel keeps the mode with the tty, whichever node it was opened through, so a board held in a container is refused with '... already in use by another capture ...' on the host and in other containers, and the other way round. A process with CAP_SYS_ADMIN (esptool or a helper run with sudo) is not stopped by the exclusive mode. The C helper's --list inside a container cannot see a lock held outside it (/proc/locks), so it still lists such a board, and opening it fails with 'already in use'. Sources: board.py open_serial and close_serial; capture_esp32c5.c serial_open, serial_close and port_locked.
